provenance.notes: Our contribution: the irregular 4x10 "pair-complement" base template on which the pair-partition rule is applied (the 10 block columns form 5 column pairs; each of the 4 block rows per side contains all pairs but one, so every check has weight 8; the X rows and the Z rows leave out different pairs, so a different pair has qubit degree 4 on each side; design rate 1/5); the weight-8 template census that selected it (one side's templates with rows of weight <= 8 and column degrees 3..4, X/Z pairs with even row overlaps, ranked by a permanent-vector upper bound, our generalisation of App. A of arXiv:2609.30069 to sparse templates); the couple solver that found the exponent spaces (an exact depth-first search over the pairings of every X-row/Z-row overlap that prunes a partial pairing as soon as a 4-cycle is forced, run as a large-neighbourhood search from known solutions: about 1,380 pairings, 573 distinct solution spaces up to the template's 192 automorphisms); the choice of this pairing, the lift P = 100 and this exponent draw; and the distance screening and lower-bound computation described in notes/1000-200-29.md. Construction framework, not ours: the pair-partition construction and its paired-difference equations on CPM exponents are Okada and Kasai's (arXiv:2607.14091), where they are applied to complete J x L templates; the design-rate count R = 1 - J_tot/L_stab and the permanent-vector bound are from Lee, Okada, Maskara, Kasai and Zhou (arXiv:2609.30069), whose outlook names quantum-compatible irregular templates as a natural direction; this entry is one instance in that direction. Quasi-cyclic CSS LDPC codes from circulant permutation matrices go back to Hagiwara and Imai (arXiv:quant-ph/0701020), and CSS pairs of two irregular LDPC codes were analysed by Hagiwara and Imai (arXiv:0801.1361). Board precedents of the same commutation rule at weight 8 on the complete (3,8) template include codes/912-234-22.json by @jacksongquera, codes/904-230-22.json by @vprusso (which also cites the lifted-product construction of Panteleev and Kalachev, arXiv:2111.03654) and the published codes/584-150-18.json (Okada-Kasai); our codes/990-198-17.json applies the rule to a different irregular template with weight-7 checks. In our check for codes/990-198-17.json (2026-10-22: arXiv:2607.14091, arXiv:2609.30069, the Okada-Kasai project page, web searches) we did not find a pair-partition code on an irregular template; literature novelty is not claimed. Distance: a witness-backed upper bound (confidence upper_bound), d <= 29, with a proved lower bound d >= 25. Upper side: Stern information-set decoding found weight-29 logicals on both sides and nothing lighter in 12 runs per side (30 s to 1 h each; the deepest: 2 seeds x 1 h per side, about 464000 iterations each, 29 on all four). The board's verify/heuristic_distance.py (RIS, orbit pass over 8 symmetry partitions, 400000 gf2_fast trials, seed 3) returned 'inconclusive': its lightest logicals had weight 36 (X) and 34 (Z), so at this size it did not get down to the claimed 29 and found nothing lighter. Lower side: an exhaustive branch-and-bound search (our gexact, built on the branch-and-bound of Okada and Kasai's cpm_distance, github.com/kasaikenta/pair-partition-cpm-css-codes, with roots from the GF(2)-verified Z_100 shift and an extra set-cover bound) found no logical of weight <= 24 on either side (all 10 roots per side complete), so d >= 25; the gap 25..28 is open; details in notes/1000-200-29.md.
